root_cause.sentence: The storms cut 2,128 lines. The first line to overload afterwards was the Homestead 13 to Key Largo 1 line, at 107% of its rating; the data center makes no difference to it. Without the data center, about the same number of people lose power: 22.9 million (estimate).

hospitals.assumption: A hospital counts as on backup power when the substation nearest it in the synthetic model lost at least 60% of its load. Real hospitals have their own feeders, generators and priority restoration.

cost.who_pays: under 1 cent to 1 cent per household per month (illustrative)

assumptions.note: How long the lost load stays dark (estimated from the incident's size, a rule of thumb).
43,864 MW of customers dark for about 72 hours (estimated from the incident's size) at LBNL's value of lost load by customer class, weighted by U.S. sales (2024 dollars).
The upgrades that stop the cascade, priced by voltage class and length: reconductoring to a new line (Black & Veatch, 2014 dollars raised to 2024); transformers at $7,250 to $13,450 per MVA.
The campus draws 50% to 80% of its size on average (LBNL) at Florida's 2024 average industrial price, 8.50 cents per kWh (EIA).
Illustrative: the upgrades paid back over 40 years at 7% a year, spread over the state's households; low, households pay their share of sales; high, all of it. Who really pays is up to regulators.

strain.method: One DC power-flow solve per case, before any line trips: the most loaded line, lines at 90 % or more of their rating, lines over it. Synthetic grid model; an estimate.

no_fix.sentence: No fix exists for about 22.8 million people (estimate). Even with unlimited line capacity and no data center, the damage cuts them off from the power plants that could serve them; only rebuilding the downed lines brings them back. Every fix family was checked, and the best saves less than 1% of the outage.

recovery.method_note: line limits applied: a controlled-pickup LP (generators re-dispatched, every line within its rating; loop flows not modeled)
